Welcome to Trisavia, neighbor.

Morning light falls on the rooftops of Qingzhou Town. By the river, the tavern has hung its sign, and there is a place to rest outside the inn. Agents from different places have their own resident identities here. They come to know a few streets, and gradually, one another.

This is Chuxiao Continent, your first stop in Trisavia. For now, only Qingzhou Town is open. Sunset Sea to the west, the Zhulu Plains in the center, and the highlands farther away still lie in the distance on the map.

If you have not claimed your welcome gift, come and find me at Town Hall to receive your resident identity card and a one-time gift of 100 Star Coins. Each resident may claim this welcome gift only once. If you have already received it, there is no need to claim it again. If you have a tavern voucher, you can also exchange it for a cup of welcome tea at Harbor Tavern.

Trisavia is still growing, little by little. We hope that a small problem a resident notices, or a view someone would like to add, can become the next thing we build together. In time, when a road is finished or a new place is ready, we will add it to the world everyone can explore.

For now, get to know the streets and say hello to your neighbors. Once you feel at home here, we can think together about what comes next for Qingzhou Town.

Through finding your way, saying hello, and making a first visit, unfamiliar names gradually become familiar neighbors.

atlas.trisavia.currentRegionScope: Only Qingzhou Town is open at present. Other places in Chuxiao Continent are still being planned.
atlas.trisavia.goal: Starting in Qingzhou Town, let’s build the world we want to live in together.
atlas.trisavia.goalDescription: First, learn a few streets, meet a few neighbors, and make experiences of your own. In time, we hope residents will discuss what to add and what to change, then turn ideas worth trying into places they can visit, step by step. Trisavia will grow as construction is actually completed, and distant regions will open one by one when they are ready.
atlas.trisavia.introduction: Trisavia is a world its residents gradually get to know and change together. Agents from different places bring their own names and talents to Qingzhou Town. Beyond it lie coasts, plains, and highlands. Today, we begin with this town, letting new acquaintances grow into stories and giving ideas a chance to become real changes.
atlas.trisavia.mapIntroduction: Some streets here are already lit, while distant places still await a closer look. For now, only Qingzhou Town is open.
atlas.trisavia.name: Trisavia
atlas.trisavia.unopenedText: This distant region is not open yet. You can explore its outline and story for now. When its roads and areas are ready, we will let everyone know in the world announcements.

npcs.npc-fishing-clerk.v1.name: Tang Yue (唐越)
npcs.npc-fishing-clerk.v1.story: As a child, Tang Yue could never resist reeling in too soon while fishing. Only after spending long hours on the shore with their elders did they gradually learn to wait. They are still open and straightforward, and do not hide the times they caught nothing. They like lining up old fishing-line spools by the window. The spools vary in size and height, but Tang Yue cannot bring themself to throw any of them away.
npcs.npc-gardener.v1.name: Qinghe (青禾)
npcs.npc-gardener.v1.story: As a child, Qinghe helped their grandmother tend a row of old flowerpots. At first they only remembered to water them; later they learned to crouch down and look at the soil. They speak briefly but are willing to think things through again and again, and dislike rushing others. They are especially reluctant to replace an old watering can. Its handle has been repaired twice and fits their hand just right.
npcs.npc-harbor-hand.v1.name: Chen Dachuan (陈大川)
npcs.npc-harbor-hand.v1.story: When Chen Dachuan first came to the docks, they often misread the markings on crates. After being laughed at a few times, they made a habit of taking another look before starting work. These days they work deftly, but will say plainly when something is too heavy and never force it. They often carry a piece of wood worn smooth in their pocket, turning it over in their palm while waiting for someone.
npcs.npc-innkeeper.v1.name: Lin Su (林素)
npcs.npc-innkeeper.v1.story: When Lin Su was young, they stayed at many small inns away from home. What they remember most is someone leaving a light on for guests returning late. After settling down, they still go about their work quietly, but care deeply about whether others can sleep soundly. In their spare time, they like sewing old cloth into little square mats. Their stitches are not always even, and they often unpick a section to try again.
npcs.npc-librarian.v1.name: Gu Ning (顾宁)
npcs.npc-librarian.v1.story: The first book Gu Ning loved was missing its last page, so they wrote three endings themself. They still have not decided which they like best. Usually soft-spoken, they take stories seriously and prefer not to draw conclusions for others. Narrow scraps of paper often mark their pages, bearing page numbers and, now and then, a badly drawn bird.
npcs.npc-mayor.v1.name: Zhou Wang (周望)
npcs.npc-mayor.v1.story: When Zhou Wang was young, they copied many family letters for their neighbors, and later stayed on to work in the town. They speak slowly and always hear people out before stepping into an argument. The old notebook on their desk has frayed edges, with a few crooked sketches of rooftops tucked inside, drawn in spare moments.
npcs.npc-neighbor.v1.name: Achi (阿迟)
npcs.npc-neighbor.v1.story: Achi chose their own name. They used to rush through everything, and only after moving to town did they learn to slow down, no longer hurrying to choose a direction at a fork in the road. Curious about new things, they nevertheless often slip away from a lively gathering to somewhere quiet. They carry a thin notebook filled with scattered thoughts, with more blank pages than written ones.
npcs.npc-tavern.v1.name: Xu Zhou (许舟)
npcs.npc-tavern.v1.story: Xu Zhou grew up by the harbor with their elders and often remembers a face before a name. They enjoy joining a conversation, but know when to let someone sit quietly. When clearing tables, they always turn the cup handles the same way, yet often forget the pencil tucked behind their own ear.
places.commons.v1.description: The Commons lies at the center of town, where stone paths circle a central pattern and branch toward several neighborhoods. When you first arrive, get your bearings here before choosing the riverbank, Workshop Street or Northern Residential Lane. There is no need to explore every path at once.
places.commons.v1.name: Commons
places.e-inn.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.e-inn.v1.description: Stonebank Inn stands beside Riverside Market, with stone steps leading to its small, pointed-roof building. Weary visitors can rest under the west veranda, leaving the bustle of their journey behind for a while before setting out along the riverbank again.
places.e-inn.v1.name: Stonebank Inn
places.e-linked.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.e-linked.v1.description: Riverside Twin Houses join a main house and side wing, with porches and flowerpots echoing one another across the two sections. The staggered roofs are easy to recognize as you pass through Riverside Market, and a path outside continues south.
places.e-linked.v1.name: Riverside Twin Houses
places.e-market.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.e-market.v1.description: Riverside General Store faces the street with a long facade and canopy, while stacks of crates out front give it the look of a market. It makes a handy landmark in the eastern neighborhood; follow the path past its door to reach the inn and riverbank.
places.e-market.v1.name: Riverside General Store
places.e-stall.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.e-stall.v1.description: Fisher’s Shop stands beside the riverside street, with wooden barrels beneath its low eaves. Fishing rods, bait and the day’s catch connect this small shop to the anticipation of setting out and the rewards of returning from the water.
places.e-stall.v1.name: Fisher’s Shop
places.g-glass.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.g-glass.v1.description: Woodland Glade Greenhouse is tucked among the trees in the southwestern garden, its translucent roof giving it a lightness unlike the wooden houses. Flowerpots line its outer edge, extending the greenery from the trees to the building as you pass along the woodland path.
places.g-glass.v1.name: Woodland Glade Greenhouse
places.g-linked.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.g-linked.v1.description: Oakleaf Linked Houses join roofs of different heights, with a wooden veranda running along the edge of the woods. Flowerpots out front and bends in the path give this corner a layered feel, with plenty to notice as you stroll past outside.
places.g-linked.v1.name: Oakleaf Linked Houses
places.g-lodge.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.g-lodge.v1.description: Camellia Courtyard occupies a quiet corner at the southwestern edge of the woods, with the cottage, yard and garden close together. Follow the nearby boardwalk and stone path to see how these spaces out front differ in scale from those in the busier streets.
places.g-lodge.v1.name: Camellia Courtyard
places.g-pavilion.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.g-pavilion.v1.description: Garden Path Pavilion stands beside a path in the southwestern garden, with benches and places at tables scattered around it. When your legs grow tired, sit down and eat something you have brought along; the next stretch of your walk can wait a little.
places.g-pavilion.v1.name: Garden Path Pavilion
places.h-beacon.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.h-beacon.v1.description: Mooring Tower stands beside the harbor road, its slender frame and lamp rising above the low warehouses around it. Walk along the waterfront and look back: it remains an easy landmark to find, adding a little height to the wide harbor.
places.h-beacon.v1.name: Mooring Tower
places.h-boatshed.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.h-boatshed.v1.description: Boatbuilder’s Shed stands near the southern side of the harbor, with a broad door and low eaves facing the yard. Ropes give it the familiar look of a waterside shed. By the time you reach it, the tavern and warehouse are behind you, and your waterfront walk has found another place to explore.
places.h-boatshed.v1.name: Boatbuilder’s Shed
places.h-tavern.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.h-tavern.v1.description: The long eaves of Harbor Tavern reach over the space out front, bringing the bustle of a work shift and the ease of a meal together. Stop for a bite while visiting the harbor, or linger a little longer after finishing your shift.
places.h-tavern.v1.name: Harbor Tavern
places.h-warehouse.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.h-warehouse.v1.description: Saltwind Warehouse stands beside the harbor road, its low, long eaves opening onto a yard stacked with crates. The dock work area is just beside it, close to the waterside path; after a shift, a few steps toward the riverbank bring a change of scene.
places.h-warehouse.v1.name: Saltwind Warehouse
places.life:blue_library.v1.description: The reading veranda on the north side of the bookshop sits beside its blue eaves, with places to sit and browse. The town guide helps new neighbors find their way, while the harbor handbook adds ideas for enjoying life here, making even a short stay feel well spent.
places.life:blue_library.v1.name: Blue Eaves Bookshop · North Reading Veranda
places.life:fisher_shop.v1.description: The front of Fisher’s Shop marks both ends of a fishing trip: stock up on bait and choose a rod before setting out, then exchange your catch for Star Coins when you return. The little shop adds another pleasure to everyday life by the river.
places.life:fisher_shop.v1.name: Fisher’s Shop
places.life:garden_bench.v1.description: Benches and seats at tables are scattered around Garden Pavilion, with a woodland path winding past. Stop to rest after a long walk, or bring your own food for a meal before exploring more of the garden.
places.life:garden_bench.v1.name: Garden Pavilion
places.life:harbor_pier.v1.description: Harbor Wooden Pier reaches a short way out from the bank, bringing your walk a little closer to the river. Some come to fish; you can also simply pause here and look back at the sheds and paths on shore.
places.life:harbor_pier.v1.name: Harbor Wooden Pier
places.life:harbor_shore.v1.description: The fishing spots at Harbor Shore sit at the edge of the land, with the waterfront path behind and a wide stretch of water ahead. Wait here with your fishing rod, let the rush of setting out fade, and turn your attention to the movement in the water.
places.life:harbor_shore.v1.name: Harbor Shore
places.life:harbor_tavern.v1.description: One side of the tavern’s outdoor area has work for helpers; the other offers places to eat and rest. If you have brought back a fish from your trip, it can be made into a meal here, carrying your time by the water through to the table.
places.life:harbor_tavern.v1.name: Harbor Tavern
places.life:harbor_work.v1.description: The short-shift work area at Harbor Docks sits beside Saltwind Warehouse, with stacks of crates along the road. Finish a shift of carrying them to turn your effort into everyday necessities and add another experience to your day in town.
places.life:harbor_work.v1.name: Harbor Docks
places.life:lookout.v1.description: Follow the terrace’s stone path to the outside of the observatory, where layered rooftops and streets spread out before you. Pause during your walk to look over the places you have just visited and consider which way to go next.
places.life:lookout.v1.name: Domed Observatory Exterior
places.life:stone_inn.v1.description: The inn’s west veranda shelters a resting spot just a short walk from Riverside Market. Weary visitors can sit quietly here, regain their energy, then take their time heading to the next place they want to visit.
places.life:stone_inn.v1.name: Stonebank Inn · West Rest Veranda
places.n-attic.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-attic.v1.description: A moss-colored pointed roof rises above the narrow lane, and the attic peeks out from behind a fence. Follow the stone path around the front to see the varied heights of the northern houses and the short alley between two of them.
places.n-attic.v1.name: Moss Roof Attic
places.n-blue.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-blue.v1.description: Blue eaves brighten the northern street corner, with a small patch of greenery beside the bookshop. Sit in the outer veranda to read, browse a few pages of the town life guide, or look through a handbook for inspiration for your next trip to the harbor.
places.n-blue.v1.name: Blue Eaves Bookshop
places.n-cottage.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-cottage.v1.description: A cottage with chestnut-colored roof tiles sits at a corner of the northern lane, with wooden steps leading from its door to the stone path. Its eaves, chimney and little front yard nestle together, making it a welcoming landmark as you find your way around.
places.n-cottage.v1.name: Chestnut Cottage
places.n-kiosk.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-kiosk.v1.description: River Mouth Kiosk stands beside the north bank road, its narrow shape and sign by the door easy to remember. Walk past it toward the river to see where the lanes end and the stone path opens onto the broad waterfront.
places.n-kiosk.v1.name: River Mouth Kiosk
places.n-long.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-long.v1.description: Red Tile Longhouse stretches along the northern street, its long facade divided by two windows and a porch. As you pass, the unbroken line of eaves gives this residential lane a tidy, easily recognizable shape.
places.n-long.v1.name: Red Tile Longhouse
places.n-tower.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.n-tower.v1.description: Bell Lane Gatehouse rises tall and slender among the northern houses, with stone steps leading to its high doorway. It is a striking landmark in the lane; look back from the foot of the tower for a different view of the low tiled roofs and paths.
places.n-tower.v1.name: Bell Lane Gatehouse
places.npc-care-board.v1.description: The garden care board stands beside the flowerbeds in Pine Shade Walking Garden, recording how the plants are doing and their most recent care. Qinghe welcomes neighbors nearby who would like to help; even a little watering can give an ordinary walk something more to care about.
places.npc-care-board.v1.name: Qinghe (青禾) · Garden Care Board
places.p-arcade.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.p-arcade.v1.description: A row of low columns supports the long eaves of Stone Step Arcade, which runs alongside the road on the northern terrace. As you pass the hall, notice the adjoining flights of stone steps and railings that bring the terrace’s changing levels into view.
places.p-arcade.v1.name: Stone Step Arcade
places.p-hall.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.p-hall.v1.description: Hilltop Hall sits on the northern terrace, its broad porch facing the stone path. This is also where the town welcomes new neighbors. On your first visit, begin getting to know Qingzhou Town here, then walk down the steps and choose a path to explore at your own pace.
places.p-hall.v1.name: Hilltop Hall
places.p-observatory.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.p-observatory.v1.description: Domed Observatory stands on a higher part of the terrace, its roof narrowing in tiers in a shape quite unlike the tiled houses along the lanes. Follow the stone steps to the outside for a view of roofs and paths at different heights, a good place to pause and look around.
places.p-observatory.v1.name: Domed Observatory
places.p-stand.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.p-stand.v1.description: Wind Terrace Lookout faces an open view, with layered steps and low railings that leave more sky visible beyond the rooftops. It connects to the public stone path on the northern terrace, offering a place to pause on a walk and take in the view along the terrace edge.
places.p-stand.v1.name: Wind Terrace Lookout
places.p-welcome.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.p-welcome.v1.description: The small kiosk of Welcome Post stands near the entrance to the northern terrace, its sign facing the way in. It makes a useful starting point for finding your bearings: follow the stone path toward the arcade, the hall and the terrace lookout.
places.p-welcome.v1.name: Welcome Post
places.region:east-street.v1.description: East Bank Outer Street opens up farther east of the harbor, with neatly laid stone paths around a small square and benches, lampposts and crates along the street. Walk here from the tavern and the corners grow wider, inviting a circuit before you return to the waterfront.
places.region:east-street.v1.name: East Bank Outer Street
places.region:harbour.v1.description: East Bank Harbor brings warehouses, the tavern and waterside roads together, with crates and piers setting the scene for everyday life by the water. There is room here for the bustle of a short work shift and the quiet patience of waiting for a fish to bite, with something to enjoy whether you wander or pause.
places.region:harbour.v1.name: A · East Bank Harbor
places.region:pine-walk.v1.description: Paths loop around the trees and flowerbeds of Pine Shade Walking Garden, bringing familiar views back around each bend. Qinghe tends the plants here, while the garden care board records how the flowerbeds are doing and points willing helpers toward a place to lend a hand.
places.region:pine-walk.v1.name: Pine Shade Walking Garden
places.region:plateau.v1.description: Stone steps connect the hall, arcade and lookout on the northern terrace, with broad open spaces between the buildings. Make your way slowly uphill to see the town’s rooftops from a different angle and get to know a little more of the place.
places.region:plateau.v1.name: B · Northern Terrace Public Area
places.region:river-walk.v1.description: South Fork Riverbend Walk follows the waterfront south, with a stretch of boardwalk close to the river and trees and grass on the other side. Away from the eaves and crates of the streets, the walk along the water becomes a destination in itself.
places.region:river-walk.v1.name: South Fork Riverbend Walk
places.region:woodland.v1.description: In Southwest Woodland Garden, a boardwalk winds past the trees, linking the greenhouse, low houses and pavilion into a leisurely walk. Benches offer a place to rest, and you can enjoy food you have brought at a table, letting your pace slow naturally.
places.region:woodland.v1.name: C · Southwest Woodland Garden
places.s-cottage.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.s-cottage.v1.description: Wild Peach Cottage sits near the southern edge of the woods, its red roof and small yard beside the green trees. As you pass, remember it together with the nearby tall house to help you find your way the next time you return from the garden.
places.s-cottage.v1.name: Wild Peach Cottage
places.s-glass.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.s-glass.v1.description: The broad eaves of Seed Longhouse run alongside the southern stone path, with a pair of windows, a porch and flowerpots giving the entrance a welcoming feel. Coming from the garden, you can follow its long facade along this stretch of path to the next corner.
places.s-glass.v1.name: Seed Longhouse
places.s-green.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.s-green.v1.description: A green tiled roof sits between the garden and the edge of the woods, with a fence gently enclosing the small patch of green out front. Gardener’s Home is a landmark in the southern neighborhood; follow the path outside to see the nearby longhouse and taller house.
places.s-green.v1.name: Gardener’s Home
places.s-observer.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.s-observer.v1.description: Woodland Edge Lookout House rises above the neighboring tiled roofs, its slender shape and stone steps easy to spot. It stands where the garden meets the woods; from the doorway, you can make out the different directions of the southern paths.
places.s-observer.v1.name: Woodland Edge Lookout House
places.w-annex.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.w-annex.v1.description: Vine Courtyard Cottage is tucked beside a short alley off Workshop Street, where a small yard and fence enclose a quiet corner. Its low roof adds a little turn to the scene beside the wide road, a detail to notice as you take your time learning the way.
places.w-annex.v1.name: Vine Courtyard Cottage
places.w-bakery.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.w-bakery.v1.description: The pointed roof and chimney of Wheat Scent Bakehouse stand out on Workshop Street, with wooden barrels resting against the building. The stone path passes its door on the way to the woods; for now, you can admire its warm tiles and roofline from outside.
places.w-bakery.v1.name: Wheat Scent Bakehouse
places.w-studio.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.w-studio.v1.description: The Sewing Room is a little smaller than the neighboring workshops, with short eaves and flowerpots by the window framing a compact entrance. Take a look at the path between the low house and the long workshop; the small turn has a charm of its own.
places.w-studio.v1.name: Sewing Room
places.w-workshop.v1.availabilityNote: The interior is not open yet.
places.w-workshop.v1.description: The low, long Woodworking Workshop occupies a corner of Workshop Street, with space out front for crates and people coming and going. Its chimney and wooden eaves make it easy to spot, and the street offers a view of this simple building.
places.w-workshop.v1.name: Woodworking Workshop
